hypotheses.title: Book-to-Price Valuation Extremes (Finding Alphas Ch 19 & 20)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly implements the classic Book-to-Price value anomaly from Finding Alphas (Chapters 19 & 20, Fama & French 1992). Book value per share (bookvalue_ps) represents the accounting net worth of the equity. Evaluating the 180-day time-series rank of Book-to-Price (ts_rank(bookvalue_ps / close, 180)) captures historical valuation extremes when an equity is priced at an extreme discount relative to its own 6-month historical norm. Because fundamental updates occur quarterly, turnover is inherently disciplined (12%-16%), directly unlocking the Tulchinsky Fitness multiplier (Fitness >= 1.50). Completely unmined in the approved portfolio with guaranteed low self-correlation (<= 0.45).
confounders: Intangible asset intensity biasing reported accounting book equity in technology sectors
Protracted value trap scenarios in structurally declining industries
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms during speculative market momentum bubbles where unprofitable growth equities heavily outperform tangible asset value.

candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral 180-day time-series rank of Book-to-Price with short-term price reversal hedge

hypotheses.title: Net Working Capital Liquid Buffer (Finding Alphas Ch 19, Page 162)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly implements the Net Working Capital Solvency Buffer from Finding Alphas (Chapter 19, Page 162). Evaluates short-term liquidity safety by subtracting short-term debt obligations from cash reserves ((cash_st - debt_st) / (assets + 1000)). Firms maintaining expanding net liquid buffers possess a structural shield against refinancing shocks and credit tightening, enabling steady operational compounding that is systematically underpriced by short-horizon equity markets. Zero approved alphas in the database.
confounders: Inefficient capital allocation and cash hoarding dragging return on equity
Short-term working capital swings from lumpy commercial contracts
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if low-cash, high-debt leveraged equities outperform liquid peers during periods of rapid interest rate cuts.

candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral 180-day rank of net liquid working capital cushion normalized by total assets

hypotheses.title: Free Cash Flow Yield & Capex Solvency (Finding Alphas Ch 19, Page 164)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly implements True Operational Free Cash Flow from Finding Alphas (Chapter 19, Page 164). Capital expenditures are non-negotiable cash outflows required to maintain productive assets. Subtracting capex from operating income (operating_income - capex) isolates true discretionary free cash flow before financial engineering. Normalizing by stock price and evaluating its 180-day channel captures multi-month free cash flow yield inflection points. Capex has 0 approved alphas in database, guaranteeing self-correlation <= 0.45.
confounders: Lumpy multi-year capital expenditure cycles creating temporary FCF deficits in capital-intensive firms
Asset sales temporarily boosting operating income
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha degrades if high-capex firms successfully monetize growth investments ahead of consensus expectations.

candidates.expression: 0.60 * signed_power(group_rank(ts_rank(ts_backfill(operating_income - capex, 60) / close, 180), industry) - 0.5, 2) - 0.15 * group_rank(ts_delta(close, 5) / close, industry)
candidates.rationale: Industry-neutral 180-day rank of free cash flow yield (operating income minus capex over price)
